newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dismal Q1 gold results hit Kloof, others.
newsitem.headline: Dismal Q1 gold results hit Kloof, others.

text.p: Dismal first quarter results knocked Kloof Gold Mining Co Ltd to a new year low on Thursday and analysts and dealers said this did not bode well for other gold mining shares.
Kloof fell to 31.75 rand per share from its previous 32.90 rand close before climbing back to 32.00 rand.
"I would think this would be very worrying for other gold shares," said Nick Goodwin, analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.
Dealers said there had already been some negative reaction from mining shares not in the Gold Fields stable.
Kloof halved its March quarter pre-capex profit to 54.63 million rand.
Parent Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd declared first quarter profit of 236.42 million rand -- a severe drop from its preceding quarter's 333.08 million rand.
But Gold Fields itself remained unmoved, not trading all day except for one trade of 200,000 shares shortly after its results which held the share steady at 108 rand.
Driefontein Consolidated fell 45 cents to 40.80 rand after it posted a fall in profit to 182.02 million rand from 214.09 million rand.
